topic.angle: A dull taxi number that is not dull

card.title: The taxi number that wasn't boring

panels.text: Once, the mathematician G. H. Hardy visits his friend Srinivasa Ramanujan, who is ill in hospital.
Hardy mentions that his taxi had a rather dull number: 1729.
Ramanujan answers at once: no, it is a very interesting number. It is the smallest number that can be written as a sum of two cubes in two different ways.
The twist: it is 1³ + 12³ and also 9³ + 10³. Numbers like this are now called taxicab numbers.

probes.question: 1729 is the smallest number that is the sum of two cubes in ____ different ways.
True or false: Hardy called 1729 a very interesting number.

claims.claim: Ramanujan said it is a very interesting number, the smallest sum of two cubes in two different ways (panel 3, probe 1)

claims.note: "At once" is not in the source; harmless narration.

claims.claim: Such numbers are called taxicab numbers (panel 4)
claims.quote: This conversation led to the definition of the taxicab number as the smallest integer that can be expressed as a sum of two positive cubes in a given number of distinct ways.
